text: I have always enjoyed listening to elders tell stories.
The same story often changes depending on who tells it.
That difference interests me.
Many old villagers remember the Night of Ash differently.
Some describe fire.
Some describe light.
Some describe sounds.
Very few describe the same event.
Nara once told me that memory is fragile.
I think she was right.
Children often repeat stories they do not understand.
Those stories sometimes contain unusual details.
Several children have independently described 'stairs in the sky'.
None could explain where they heard the phrase.
The oldest songs contain words nobody understands.
Those words appear in more than one song.
The monument appears in nearly every village legend.
Yet nobody agrees on its purpose.
Some stories claim it was a temple.
Others claim it was a city.
Others claim it was built by giants.
I do not believe the giant story.
Elira remembers details most villagers ignore.
People dismiss her too quickly.
My grandfather once told me: 'The village was built around a promise.'
He died before explaining what promise he meant.
Many villagers possess heirlooms they cannot explain.
Families rarely discuss where those heirlooms came from.
The small ancient building contains carvings of people carrying objects.
Several objects resemble heirlooms still found in the village.
